method: A sweep of every page of the year for passages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains; each passage read, looked up in the year's lists and counted by its own opening words against every page in both transcriptions, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN as amended on 23 November 2026: items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news counted by their own words, C-09); the items printed by every surviving paper admitted at the owner's word of 25 November 2026; scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: New York, 23 July 1783: 'Last Monday arrived here the brig Lucy ... from St. Kitts' with a report of the definitive treaty, and 'his majesty's frigate Mercury' from Spithead
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph of the New York news of 23 July 1783: 'Last Monday arrived here the brig Lucy, captain Van Duersen, in twelve days from St. Kitts, bound to Connecticut; from which a report prevails, that the day before he sailed, dispatches were received from Barbadoes, with an account of the definitive treaty being signed ...' and 'Same day arrived from Spithead, his majesty's frigate Mercury, of 28 guns ...', with government's dispatches. A New York report of two arrivals, as the papers reprinted it; the New-Hampshire Gazette prints only the part on the frigate Mercury (C-02).
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1783 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1783. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1783 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found one item printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit it as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted. The New York paragraph of 23 July is printed by all 4 papers of its weeks, one of them in part (C-02).

counted_item_by_item.The New York report of the brig Lucy and: 4 of the 4 papers that survive for its weeks (PP 26 July, CC 5 August, SCG 6 August, NHG 9 August); by its opening (the brig Lucy) 3 of 4, and the New-Hampshire Gazette prints only its part on the frigate Mercury, under the same date 'July 23.', counted with the others as an abridged print (C-02).
